hints: Since the $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ forces are perpendicular, choose axes along these two forces: let the $6\text{ N}$ force act along the positive $x$-axis and the $8\text{ N}$ force along the positive $y$-axis.
For equilibrium, the resultant of the $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ forces must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the $10\text{ N}$ force.

Let $\alpha$ be the angle between the line of action of the $10\text{ N}$ force and the negative $y$-axis (or negative $x$-axis), and resolve along the axes: $10\cos\alpha = 8$ and $10\sin\alpha = 6$.

Calculate $\alpha$, then determine the angles between the $10\text{ N}$ force and the $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ forces by adding $90^\circ$ to the complementary angles: $90^\circ + \alpha$ and $180^\circ - \alpha$.
walkthrough:
Align coordinate axes along the perpendicular forces: let the $6\text{ N}$ force act along the positive $x$-direction and the $8\text{ N}$ force along the positive $y$-direction. For the three forces to be in equilibrium, the $10\text{ N}$ force must have components that balance both forces:
$$10\cos\alpha = 8 \quad \text{and} \quad 10\sin\alpha = 6$$
where $\alpha$ is the acute angle made by the line of the $10\text{ N}$ force with the negative $y$-axis.

Find the angle between the $8\text{ N}$ force and the $10\text{ N}$ force:
$$\theta_{8,10} = 180^\circ - \alpha = 180^\circ - 36.87^\circ = 143.13^\circ \approx 143.1^\circ$$

Find the angle between the $6\text{ N}$ force and the $10\text{ N}$ force:
$$\theta_{6,10} = 90^\circ + \alpha = 90^\circ + 36.87^\circ = 126.87^\circ \approx 126.9^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for static equilibrium of three coplanar forces:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$
Because the $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ forces are perpendicular, we set up an orthogonal coordinate frame where the $6\text{ N}$ force acts along the $+x$ direction and the $8\text{ N}$ force acts along the $+y$ direction.

Let the $10\text{ N}$ force act in the third quadrant (so both its components are negative, directly opposing the $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ forces). Let $\alpha$ be the angle between the $10\text{ N}$ force and the negative $y$-axis.
Resolving along the $y$-axis:
$$8 - 10\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$10\cos\alpha = 8$$
Divide both sides by $10$:
$$\cos\alpha = \frac{8}{10} = 0.8$$
$$\alpha = \cos^{-1}(0.8) \approx 36.8699^\circ$$

The angle between the positive $y$-axis (the $8\text{ N}$ force) and the $10\text{ N}$ force is supplementary to $\alpha$:
$$\theta_{8,10} = 180^\circ - \alpha$$
Substitute $\alpha = 36.8699^\circ$:
$$\theta_{8,10} = 180^\circ - 36.8699^\circ = 143.1301^\circ \approx 143.1^\circ$$

The angle between the positive $x$-axis (the $6\text{ N}$ force) and the $10\text{ N}$ force consists of a right angle ($90^\circ$) plus the angle $\alpha$:
$$\theta_{6,10} = 90^\circ + \alpha$$
Substitute $\alpha = 36.8699^\circ$:
$$\theta_{6,10} = 90^\circ + 36.8699^\circ = 126.8699^\circ \approx 126.9^\circ$$

Verify that the sum of all three angles around the point is $360^\circ$:
$$90^\circ + 143.1301^\circ + 126.8699^\circ = 360^\circ$$
